newsitem.title: ITALY: Berisha says new Albanian govt in 24 hours-Italy.
newsitem.headline: Berisha says new Albanian govt in 24 hours-Italy.

text.p: Albanian President Sali Berisha told Italy on Tuesday that he had selected a new prime minister and that a new government would be formed within 24 hours, the Italian Foreign Ministry said.
A ministry official said Berisha, who is facing spreading insurgency in his Balkan state, had conveyed the news in a telephone call to Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini.

"President Berisha has informed Minister Dini that he has already chosen the new prime minister and that the new government will be established within 24 hours," the official said. He was unable to provide further details.

Berisha, his ruling Democratic Party and nine opposition parties signed an accord at the weekend to establish a national unity government and hold early elections by June in an attempt to find a political solution to the insurrection.

Dini has been spearheading international diplomatic efforts to help restore calm to impoverished Albania, where popular anger at the loss of savings in the collapse of shady pyramid savings schemes has mushroomed into insurrection.

Political parties in Tirana agreed on Monday to split cabinet posts evenly between the Democratic Party and the opposition. However the two sides have been deadlocked on who gets the key portfolios, political sources said.
